title: Link-middle-cut lower bounds for Clifford circuit synthesis
abstract: Minimizing the number of CNOT gates required to synthesize a Clifford operator is a central problem in quantum circuit optimization. We extend the link--middle--cut (LMC) framework for linear reversible circuits to Clifford operators represented by binary symplectic tableaux. By introducing block-support connectivity graphs and determinantal invariants, we obtain efficiently computable lower bounds on ancilla-free CNOT complexity. We prove that these bounds are tight for qubit permutations: a permutation of $n$ qubits with $k$ cycles requires exactly $3(n-k)$ CNOT gates, even when arbitrary one-qubit Clifford gates are available. We also derive efficiently computable bounds for synthesis up to a permutation of the output qubits, corresponding to free qubit relabeling. Finally, we further demonstrate the utility of the bound by using it as an admissible heuristic for $A^*$-based Clifford synthesis and show that, on benchmark instances, the resulting search can prove optimality beyond what was possible with earlier SAT-based methods, and that it may be used in combination with earlier $A^*$ heuristics to improve the CNOT counts obtained through heuristic search.
summary: This paper develops advanced mathematical tools to find lower bounds on the minimum number of CNOT gates needed to implement any Clifford quantum circuit. By extending the Link-Middle-Cut framework to use symplectic tableaux, the authors derive multiple, computable invariants. These bounds are shown to be tight for simple cases like qubit permutations and significantly improve heuristic search algorithms for quantum circuit optimization.
main_problem: The central problem is minimizing the number of CNOT gates required to synthesize a given Clifford operator on $n$ qubits.
main_result: The authors derive efficiently computable lower bounds for the CNOT complexity using an extension of the Link-Middle-Cut (LMC) framework, proving tightness for qubit permutations as $3(n-k)$.
method: The method extends the LMC framework by mapping the problem to symplectic tableaux and introducing block-support connectivity graphs and determinantal invariants to establish rigorous lower bounds.
model_or_system: The system is an $n$-qubit quantum circuit implementing Clifford operators, which are analyzed using the mathematical structure of the symplectic group $	ext{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{F}_2)$ via symplectic tableaux.
key_observables: CNOT-complexity (minimum CNOT count), link/cut invariants ($\hat{v}(F), \hat{e}(F)$), and determinantal invariants ($	ext{rank}(M(F) + I_n)$).
important_parameters: Number of qubits ($n$) and the number of cycles ($k$) in the corresponding permutation.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to extend the LMC framework from CNOT-only circuits to general Clifford operators, and it addresses the case where output qubit relabeling is free.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the link–middle–cut bound for a four-cycle permutation, explicitly calculating the required links, middles, and cuts to match the known lower bound of 9 CNOT gates.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first extending the LMC framework to Clifford operators using symplectic tableaux. It then derives multiple, efficiently computable lower bounds based on graph invariants (links/cuts) and determinantal invariants (middle contribution). Finally, it demonstrates the utility of these bounds by using them as an admissible heuristic in an A*-based search algorithm.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical tools developed (LMC extension, determinantal invariants) provide powerful, computable lower bounds for circuit synthesis, which is fundamental to understanding the efficiency limits of quantum computation.
